category_title: Reluctant readers who prioritize digital reading as a means to avoid traditional academic tasks
student_description: This student is a reluctant reader who uses digital reading (e-readers) primarily as an escape from traditional English coursework. They experience task resistance when faced with regular assignments but can achieve reading flow if given dedicated, uninterrupted reading time. They uniquely require reading to be positioned as a post-work reward and need accountability measures to be extremely low-stakes to avoid triggering their aversion to 'English work.'

criteria.rationale: This student requires extended, uninterrupted reading periods without concurrent assignments to overcome reluctance and experience reading flow.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must incorporate dedicated, full-session reading periods (e.g., weekly SSR) where the sole focus is reading without simultaneous academic tasks.

criteria.rationale: Traditional English assignments trigger task resistance for this student, so accountability must be brief and highly structured to avoid ruining the appeal of reading.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must use brief, low-effort accountability measures (such as Likert scales or short open-ended reflections) rather than traditional, heavy academic assignments.
